findings.reason: The protected source is already concise expert-interview code. `pieces_needed`, `candidate`, `pieces`, and `current` expose the maximin feasibility test directly, while `low` and `high` implement a conventional last-feasible-value search without unnecessary abstraction. A candidate would not materially improve readability, structure, correctness, or complexity.

For any candidate minimum, positive chunk values make the earliest qualifying boundary greedy-optimal: it leaves at least as much suffix sweetness for later pieces and therefore maximizes the qualifying piece count. At least `k + 1` pieces is sufficient because surplus adjacent pieces can be merged without reducing any piece below the candidate. The feasibility predicate is monotone, `min(sweetness)` is feasible, `sum(sweetness) // (k + 1)` is an upper bound, and upper-midpoint updates converge to the greatest feasible value.

An independent exact partition dynamic program computed the best minimum over prefix and piece-count states, and direct cut enumeration cross-checked small bars. Oracle, protected app source, immutable native source, and a separately written pseudo-polynomial candidate scan agreed on all ten ordinary cases, all three benchmark tiers, 21,324 exhaustive bars over values 1, 2, and 4 for lengths one through seven and every legal `k`, and 5,000 deterministic schema-valid random bars generated with seed 1231.

Visible fixtures preserve all three authenticated source examples and cover no cuts, one chunk per piece, balanced and uneven partitions, dominant interior sweetness, surplus greedy pieces, both numeric sweetness endpoints, and the minimum array length. Deterministic random validation covered 1,327 no-cut inputs, 1,327 maximum-cut inputs, 2,799 interior-cut inputs, 969 inputs containing sweetness one, 1,357 balanced optima, 1,119 dominant chunks, 453 minimum-length bars, and 412 length-twelve bars. Separate length-10,000 checks covered all-minimum and all-maximum values with no, maximum, and interior cut counts.

All ten correctness cases are visible and remain separate from the three hidden performance-only tiers. The tiers use positive unique sizes 8, 32, and 129 and exercise both the full feasibility scan and a growing answer-search range. Protected passed the final scaling run at 0.99x reference time, an independently written optimal control passed at 1.15x, and the correct pseudo-polynomial scan preserved all thirteen outputs but failed only scaling in three runs at 34.52x, 38.28x, and 35.65x with extra growth exponents from +1.02 through +1.06. Benchmark calibration is healthy and `benchmark.json` remains unchanged.

Metadata consistently identifies Premium LeetCode algorithm problem 1231, Python, and native entrypoint `Solution.maximizeSweetness`. The branch manifest now uses the repository-required plain notation `O(n log(S / (k + 1)))` instead of a LaTeX command string; the bound itself is unchanged. The protected contract remains `solve(sweetness, k)` with exactly `k` cuts into `k + 1` nonempty contiguous pieces and an integer maximin return.

The immutable native source remains bound to verified submission 2067965292 and is unchanged. Apart from the required `Solution.maximizeSweetness` wrapper and type-only `List` syntax, it and the protected app source share the exact piece target, lower and upper search bounds, upper midpoint, greedy accumulation and reset, feasibility branch, and final return.

The Approach was reviewed as part of the expert-quality pass and exactly matches the protected code: earliest qualifying cuts, the surplus-piece merging proof, monotone feasibility, minimum-chunk lower bound, average upper bound, upper-midpoint last-feasible search, and scalar workspace. Its `O(n log(S / (k + 1)))` time and `O(1)` auxiliary-space analysis is accurate for total sweetness `S`.

The modular Reference preserves the ordered-chunk model, exactly `k` cuts, `k + 1` nonempty contiguous pieces, the maximum possible minimum sweetness, all three source examples in order with their explanations, both constraints, and all three hints. It introduces no image, table, note, follow-up, or fabricated source section.

A fresh authenticated Premium review confirmed three examples with explanations, two constraints, three hints, and no image, table, note, or follow-up. `source_fidelity.json` binds all five modular files to live statement hash cfbea49a0f1e3f1191c50c2c06869d9a42178fe415d78cd9a14d2e52f3024189.
